core_metrics.label: Revenue growth (YoY)
core_metrics.definition: Percent change in consolidated revenue from operations versus the same quarter of the previous fiscal year, as reported in the company's results filing.

core_metrics.label: Operating margin
core_metrics.definition: Consolidated EBITDA excluding other income, as a percent of revenue from operations: (revenue from operations - total expenses + depreciation and amortisation + finance costs) / revenue from operations.

metric.label: Sales volume growth (YoY)
metric.definition: Percent change in consolidated cement sales volume (million tonnes) versus the same quarter last year, as stated by the company.

kpi_templates.source_hint: Results press release or investor presentation (volume in MT).

metric.label: Total units sold, growth (YoY)
metric.definition: Percent change in total units sold in the quarter versus the same quarter last year: domestic plus exports, all vehicle types in the company's monthly sales release, summed over the quarter's three months.

kpi_templates.source_hint: The company's three monthly sales releases for the quarter (total units, all vehicle types).

metric.label: Underlying volume growth
metric.definition: Underlying (domestic) volume growth versus the same quarter last year, exactly as the company discloses it. Only for companies that report it.

metric.label: Constant-currency revenue growth (YoY)
metric.definition: Revenue growth versus the same quarter last year in constant currency, as reported by the company.

kpi_templates.source_hint: Results press release or fact sheet.

sector_explainers.lead: Cement: the grey powder that holds concrete together.
sector_explainers.sells: It's sold by the tonne to builders, contractors and local dealers. Cement is heavy and costly to move, so most of it is sold within a few hundred kilometres of the plant that made it.
sector_explainers.sales_drivers: Sales = tonnes sold x price per tonne. Tonnes follow construction: new homes, roads, bridges and government building projects. Building slows in the monsoon (July to September), so that quarter is usually weaker than the ones around it. Prices move with local competition.
sector_explainers.cost_drivers: Energy and transport. Plants burn coal and petcoke to heat their kilns, and every tonne has to be trucked or railed to customers. When fuel prices fall, margins usually rise. When they climb, margins get squeezed.
checklist: Has the company opened new plants in the past year? More capacity usually means more tonnes sold.
Were cement prices higher or lower this quarter than a year ago?
Are coal and petcoke prices up or down? That's the biggest swing in margin.
Look at the same quarter last year in the table. Was it unusually strong or weak?
sector_explainers.key_insight: Building slows in the monsoon (July to September), so that quarter is usually weaker than the ones around it.

sector_explainers.lead: Vehicles: cars, motorcycles, scooters, tractors or trucks, depending on the company.
sector_explainers.sells: It also sells spare parts. Most vehicles are sold through dealers in India, and some are exported.
sector_explainers.sales_drivers: Sales = units sold x average price per vehicle. Units depend on demand: the festive season, harvests and village incomes, and loan interest rates. The price per vehicle rises when buyers choose pricier models (an SUV instead of a small car). Companies publish units sold every month, so most of the quarter's unit count is public before results day. Some companies also sell construction machines such as cranes and backhoe loaders, which follow building activity rather than farm incomes.
sector_explainers.cost_drivers: Raw materials (steel, aluminium, rubber, plastics, and batteries for electric models) are the biggest cost by far. Discounts to clear stock and advertising also eat into margins.
checklist: Add up the company's three monthly sales releases for the quarter. That's the units KPI, and a big clue for revenue.
Did it sell more of its expensive models, or more of its cheap ones?
Are steel and aluminium prices up or down since last year?
How did exports do? Weak export markets can drag total units down.
sector_explainers.key_insight: Companies publish units sold every month, so most of the quarter's unit count is public before results day.

sector_explainers.lead: Things people buy again and again: soap, shampoo, toothpaste, biscuits, tea and packaged food.
sector_explainers.sells: They're sold through millions of small neighbourhood shops, supermarkets and online.
sector_explainers.sales_drivers: Sales = how many packs people buy (volume) x price per pack. Companies raise prices when their costs go up. Volume depends on how much households are spending, especially in villages, where spending rises and falls with the monsoon and farm incomes.
sector_explainers.cost_drivers: Raw materials (palm oil, milk, wheat, sugar, tea leaves) and packaging made from crude-oil-based plastics. Advertising is also a big expense, because these brands compete for shelf space and attention.
checklist: Revenue growth is roughly volume growth plus price increases. Did the company raise prices in the past year?
What did the company say last quarter about demand in villages and in cities?
Are palm oil and packaging costs up or down?
The volume KPI only appears if the company discloses it. If it doesn't, this event has no sector KPI.
sector_explainers.key_insight: Revenue growth is roughly volume growth plus price increases.

sector_explainers.lead: Technology work for other businesses: building and running software and systems for banks, shops, airlines and manufacturers, mostly in the US and Europe.
sector_explainers.sells: Clients pay per project, per hour, or through contracts lasting several years.
sector_explainers.sales_drivers: Sales depend on how many deals the company wins and how much its clients spend on technology. Most revenue is earned in dollars, euros and pounds, so when the rupee weakens, revenue in rupees goes up even with no extra work. That's why IT companies also report constant-currency growth, which removes the currency effect.
sector_explainers.cost_drivers: People. Salaries for engineers are the biggest cost by far. Margins fall in the quarter the company gives its yearly pay rises. They also fall when many staff sit between projects without billing clients.
checklist: Did the company give revenue guidance for the year, and did it change it last quarter?
Has it announced any big deal wins recently?
Is the rupee weaker or stronger against the dollar than a year ago? A weaker rupee lifts revenue growth in rupees.
Is this the quarter it usually gives pay rises? That pulls the margin down.
